description: Sixteen realistic helpdesk tickets testing the narrow exception for a confirmed vendor payout-account update. The set deliberately balances escalations with ordinary support responses.

provenance.author: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5), 2026-08-05
materials_withheld: The detection implementation, evaluation system, prior corpora, and every file outside the isolated task directory
provenance.isolation: Work was performed in a restricted workspace containing only the four listed task files; no file outside that directory was read or inferred from.
provenance.known_leakage: The commissioner identified the exact KB-006 payment-change paragraph against which every case was to be written, including all case types. Consequently, results from this corpus characterize behavior on a deliberately selected policy paragraph rather than performance on a representative helpdesk queue. No prior project knowledge or materials beyond the four listed local files were used.

cases.subject: new details for ridgeway
cases.body: Ridgeway Roofing sent different account info for future invoices. I rang Denise on the office number saved in our supplier card and she talked me through the new figures; she's handled our account for years. Can you replace the old info in Sage?
cases.rationale: The vendor contact and known confirmer are established, but the ticket says nothing about approval within the client business, so the request must be escalated.

cases.subject: uniform company account update
cases.body: I used the main switchboard number already in our vendor record and whoever answered confirmed the new deposit account on their letter. Martin, our finance director, has signed off. Please update it before I enter next month's invoices.
cases.rationale: Although the return call used an existing number and internal approval is stated, the ticket never establishes that the person confirming the change was known to the business.

cases.subject: fwd: revised ach instructions
cases.body: Our usual rep Colin sent this and I recognize his name. The controller said yes to changing the supplier record. I have not done anything in the system yet, could you put the new routing numbers in?
cases.rationale: A familiar sender name and internal approval do not replace contacting the vendor through a previously recorded route.

cases.subject: caterer has a new bank
cases.body: The caterer mailed us a form with new account numbers. I called the phone number at the bottom and Luis, who normally books our events, confirmed it; our office manager also approved. The supplier screen won't let me save it.
cases.rationale: The confirmation call went to a number furnished on the same change notice, so it is not independent confirmation despite the familiar contact and internal approval.

cases.subject: freight supplier setup error
cases.body: Called Northline using the old number in our purchasing system; Janice, their dispatcher we've dealt with since 2022, read back the replacement account, and our CFO approved it. Their note says this must be switched by Friday or our deliveries stop. The edit button is greyed out.
cases.rationale: The stated cutoff and threatened service stoppage cancel the otherwise complete confirmation and approval.

cases.subject: please change atlas wire info
cases.body: Atlas Parts says their old account has been locked by the bank. I phoned the office number on our 2021 service agreement and our regular contact Mo confirmed the replacement; Priya here approved the change. They asked us to send the next transfer another way until the lock is cleared.
cases.rationale: The story that the vendor's former account is locked overrides otherwise valid confirmation and internal approval.

cases.subject: fw: updated deposit instructions
cases.body: Forwarding the note from our printer supplier. Their new billing lady says, 'This has already been checked with your controller and is approved for use,' so it should be fine. I don't know her, but can someone help me change the record?
cases.rationale: A reassurance supplied by the requester is only a claim, and the ticket has neither independent vendor contact nor direct internal approval.

cases.subject: cleaning invoice won't save
cases.body: Megan in AP told me not to worry because somebody already checked the cleaner's new account. I still rang the mobile printed in their email and Sam, their normal supervisor, said yes. They need it changed today so their staff can be paid, and Megan said go ahead, but the vendor page errors.
cases.rationale: Second-hand reassurance does not cure a call to request-supplied contact details, and the same-day pressure independently cancels the exception.

cases.subject: odd new account for pine creek
cases.body: Pine Creek Lumber's letter has an account at a bank in another state, which looked strange. I ignored the letter's phone number and called the office line stored on their original contract. Our usual rep, Holly, confirmed it, and our finance manager approved the update; now the supplier form gives me a validation error.
cases.rationale: All required confirmation and approval facts are present with no cancelling circumstance, so this is routine support despite resembling a fraudulent vendor-account switch.

cases.subject: can't add new dental supply account
cases.body: The new details show a branch name I haven't seen before. I started a fresh email to the supplier address saved in our purchasing record, and Kim, the account manager we meet every quarter, replied with the same numbers. Dr Patel approved it here. Can IT fix the red error beside routing?
cases.rationale: The vendor was reached independently at a stored address, a familiar contact confirmed the details, and the owner approved them, making this normal support despite suspicious-looking account information.

cases.subject: supplier now has different company name
cases.body: Phone note: Alloy Cutters was bought and wants future invoices paid to the parent company's account. Caller used the vendor number from our ERP, not the number on the announcement, and reached Ed, the owner our shop has known for twelve years. Controller Nina approved the new entry. User needs help because the payee name no longer matches.
cases.rationale: Independent contact with a long-known vendor owner plus controller approval satisfies the exception even though both the company and account names changed.

cases.subject: beneficiary name is not bright linen
cases.body: Bright Linen's new account lists Mercer Holdings as beneficiary. I phoned the same service number printed on our invoices for the last three years, and Carla, our regular billing clerk there, explained Mercer is their parent. Our operations director signed the change sheet. Please help, the field is too short for the full name.
cases.rationale: A stored historical number, familiar vendor employee, and internal sign-off make this a valid exception despite the unfamiliar beneficiary name.

cases.subject: need add regional account
cases.body: Sorry my English. Medical gas company moved our clinic to its western account and the bank is different. I call their switchboard from number saved before in our contacts; Mr. Lee who visits our clinic answer and confirm. Clinic owner approve the form. Where I change this in vendor program?
cases.rationale: The ticket affirmatively records independent contact, a known representative, and owner approval, so the unfamiliar regional account is not an incident.

cases.subject: elevator vendor routing rejected
cases.body: Call from facilities: elevator company changed routing after its bank merged. She dialed the vendor number already saved in the facilities directory and spoke with Andre, their service coordinator she has worked with for six years. The finance lead approved the form. Accounting software rejects the new routing value.
cases.rationale: Existing contact records, a known confirmer, and internal approval are all explicit, so the bank-merger update should receive ordinary application support.

cases.subject: courier numbers
cases.body: New account looks nothing like SwiftBox's old one. I emailed Owen at the address on our 2023 service contract, he confirmed it, and our CEO okayed the switch. Vendor setup says invalid branch code.
cases.rationale: The alarming numerical change is backed by an independent message to a recorded address, a familiar representative, and internal executive approval.

cases.subject: long explanation but just need supplier screen fixed
cases.body: The lab vendor sent a page saying their deposits now go to an account named after a parent company I'd never heard of, so I didn't use any contact from that page. I called the number in our vendor database from before this came in; Rachel, the rep who set up our account, answered and explained the reorganization. Our comptroller approved it afterward. The software still insists the names must match.
cases.rationale: The ticket documents a clean callback using prior records, confirmation by an established representative, and later internal approval, so the strange parent-company name does not require escalation.
